android-a11y-cli lets the agent read on-screen UI structure, perform taps and gestures, and watch system events. Both rows below must be set: pick an Agent permission and enable the Accessibility service in system Settings.

When disabled, the agent cannot read or modify app settings. The change history at Logs → Config Changes remains accessible. The agent receives a permission_denied error and can guide you through Settings.
This will reset all permission preferences. Continue?
Privileged Android APIs via the Shizuku service
android-shizuku-cli grants the agent privileged Android APIs (package install, settings put, force-stop, …) via the Shizuku service authorized over wireless ADB or root. Both rows below must be set.

android-shizuku-cli exposes the full subcommand surface: package, permission, activity, display, settings, user, network, input, notification, file, device, service. Run `android-shizuku-cli --help` from a shell to see usage.
Shizuku is running. Tap Authorize IEXA to grant access. A system dialog from Shizuku will ask you to confirm.
Opens the Play Store (or GitHub releases as fallback)
Shizuku is a free, open-source helper app from RikkaApps. Install it from Google Play, then return here.
Launch Shizuku Manager to start or manage the service
Re-poll Shizuku state after starting the service
Open the Shizuku app and start the service via wireless ADB (no PC) or root. After it shows running, return here.
Shizuku is running but IEXA is not authorized.
The Shizuku Manager app is required.
Open the Shizuku app and press Start.

Shizuku exposes privileged system APIs to user apps without root, by running a small service started via wireless ADB or root. Once authorized, IEXA can use the android-shizuku-cli CLI for package, permission, settings, input, and activity management.
